Still, the effects of salt on health have been debated. Some have argued that the increases in plasma renin activity, uric acid and
perhaps insulin resistance that occur as a result of a reduced salt intake mitigate the beneﬁcial effects of salt reduction on BP (Grau-
dal et al., 2012). However, in contrast to BP, the clinical relevance of increased plasma renin activity and uric acid is uncertain, espe-
cially because antihypertensive medications that raise plasma renin levels and uric acid actually lower cardiovascular disease risk. It
has also been argued that a reduced salt intake has little or no effect on BP in many individuals.
